stitches.name: Running Stitch
stitches.description: The most basic stitch used for seams, gathering fabric, and attaching patches.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the opposite side.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile to complete your first stitch entry.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch. The needle has emerged, completing the first running stitch.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle back down a short distance from where the thread emerged to create the second stitch.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Push the needle through and bring it up again. You now have two complete stitches visible on the front.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Continue the pattern. You can now see two complete running stitches forming a dashed line.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Repeat the process: the needle goes down, creating a stitch, and emerges to continue the pattern.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Continue stitching along your line. The front shows the characteristic dashed pattern of evenly spaced stitches.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: On the back, the stitch appears as longer thread paths. Tie a secure knot on the back to finish.

stitches.name: Backstitch
stitches.description: A strong, durable stitch ideal for repairing loose seams.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through. Cut the thread to your desired length.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the opposite side.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile to complete your first stitch entry.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: The needle emerges at point '1', completing the first stitch of the backstitch pattern.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle down at point '2', which is one stitch length behind point '1' where the thread emerged.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Push the needle through from point '2' and bring it up at point '3', which is two stitch lengths ahead of point '1'.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Pull the thread through to complete the second stitch. You now have two connected stitches forming a solid line.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Continue the pattern: insert the needle down at point '2' (end of previous stitch) and bring it up at point '3' (two lengths ahead).

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Insert the needle down at point '4', directly at the end of the previous stitch to continue the solid line.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: Bring the needle up at point '5', ahead of the previous stitches, to form the next part of the continuous line.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.text: Pull the thread through. You can now see the stitches connecting to form a solid, unbroken line on the surface.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.text: Repeat the motion: insert the needle down at point '3' and bring it up at point '5' to extend the row of stitches.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.text: Continue until the repair is complete. The finished backstitch creates a strong, solid line of evenly spaced stitches perfect for reinforcing seams.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.text: On the back, the thread forms a continuous, overlapping line. Tie off the thread securely here to finish the repair.

stitches.name: Whip Stitch
stitches.description: Used to join two edges of fabric, finish raw edges, or repair torn edges.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length, depending on the length of the repair.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch through the fabric edges.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the opposite side, pulling the thread through.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the back of the textile. Bring the needle around the edge of the fabric and insert it from back to front, creating the first whip stitch. The needle emerges at point 1 on the front side.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch. Position the needle at point 1 where the thread emerged, ready to insert it through both fabric layers.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle at point 2, a short distance from point 1, pushing it through both fabric layers from back to front.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Push the needle through and guide it around the edge of the fabric from the back, bringing it back to the front to maintain the wrapping motion.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Pull the needle through to the front, emerging at point 2. The thread wraps around the fabric edge, creating the characteristic diagonal stitch.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Continue this pattern along the entire edge. The front shows evenly spaced diagonal stitches wrapping around the fabric edge.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: On the back, the thread forms a continuous line along the edge. Tie a secure knot to finish and trim any excess thread.

stitches.name: Catch Stitch
stitches.description: A cross-stitch used for hemming and holding split fabric edges flat without puckering.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length, depending on the length of the repair.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the opposite side, pulling the thread through.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile. The needle emerges at point 1, completing your first stitch entry.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch at point 1. Position the needle at point 2 on the opposite fabric edge, ready to make the next stitch.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle at point 2, pushing it through the fabric from front to back. The needle should pass through point 3 on the opposite side.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread completely through to the back of the textile, creating a small horizontal stitch on the fabric edge.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: The needle emerges at point 3 on the front. The thread now crosses diagonally from point 1 to point 2 to point 3, forming the characteristic catch stitch pattern.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Bring the needle back to the original side, positioning it at point 4. Insert the needle, continuing the alternating pattern.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Insert the needle at point 5, pushing it through the fabric from front to back. The needle passes through point 4 on the opposite side, continuing the alternating pattern.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread completely through to the back of the textile, creating another small horizontal stitch on the fabric edge.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.text: The needle emerges at point 5 on the front. The thread crosses diagonally from point 4 to point 5, forming another X-shaped stitch.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.text: Continue this pattern along the entire edge. The front shows a series of evenly spaced, crossing stitches that hold the fabric edges flat without puckering.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.text: On the back, the thread forms small, separate stitches. Tie a secure knot to finish and trim any excess thread.

stitches.name: Ladder Stitch
stitches.description: An invisible stitch perfect for closing tiny holes seamlessly.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through. Cut the thread to your desired length.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the opposite side.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile to complete your first stitch entry.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch. The number '1' points to the loop of thread that is now visible.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle downwards at point '2', directly across from where the thread emerged at point '1'.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Push the needle through and bring it up at point '3'. You are creating a horizontal stitch across the gap.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Continue the pattern. You can now see two parallel horizontal stitches across the gap.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Repeat the process: the needle goes down at point '2', with the previous stitch at '1' and the next emergence point at '3'.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Continue alternating stitches. Pull the needle up at point '3' and push it down at point '4' to add another stitch.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: Hold the fabric edges together. You can now see the parallel stitches spanning across the gap.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.text: Continue building the stitch. The needle emerges at point '5', with previous stitches marked at '3' and '4'.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.text: A series of evenly spaced, parallel stitches are now visible across the gap, with the needle at the end of the line.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.text: On the back, the thread paths are longer and curved, connecting the points where the needle went in and out. Tie a secure knot to finish.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Identify the loose seam on the back of the textile. The damaged area shows unraveling or broken stitches that need reinforcement.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Straighten out the loose seam by gently aligning the fabric edges. Make sure the seam line is straight before you begin stitching.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length, depending on the length of the seam you need to repair.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch along the loose seam line.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: From the back, push the needle through the fabric layers to anchor your thread near the loose seam.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Turn the textile to the other side to ensure the fabric edges are aligned correctly before continuing your stitching.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: On the back, the needle emerges at point '1', marking the starting position for your row of backstitches.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Insert the needle down into the fabric a short distance ahead of point '1' to create the first part of the stitch.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Bring the needle up, then insert it back down at point '2' and '3' to create the strong, overlapping backstitch.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Continue the backstitch pattern along the seam line. Ensure the needle passes through both layers of fabric to securely reinforce the loose area.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: On the back, the needle emerges at point '3', directly adjacent to the previous stitch at point '2'. This 'back' motion is what creates the strong, continuous line.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.text: Insert the needle down at point '4', moving forward along the seam line by one stitch length from where you just emerged.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.text: Bring the needle up again at point '5', which is at the very end of the previous stitch (point '4'). You are essentially stepping back to fill the gap.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.text: Pull the thread through tightly. The back of the textile now shows a solid, unbroken line of stitching where the seam was previously loose.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.text: Continue the backstitch pattern. The needle emerges at the next point in the sequence (following points 3, 4, and 5), extending the solid line of stitching along the seam.

steps.title: Step 17
steps.text: Repeat this process until the entire loose section of the seam is covered. The back of the textile should now show a continuous, strong row of backstitches.

steps.title: Step 18
steps.text: To finish the repair, tie a secure knot on the back of the textile to fasten the thread. Trim any excess thread to complete the reinforcement.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length, depending on the length of the torn edge.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Fold the torn edges of the fabric inward to create a clean, finished edge. This will prevent further fraying.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch along the folded edge.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Push the needle through the folded fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the front side, pulling the thread through.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile. The needle emerges at point 1, completing the first whip stitch along the folded edge.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch at point 1. Position the needle at the edge of the folded fabric, ready to make the next stitch.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Insert the needle at point 2, a short distance from point 1, pushing it through the folded fabric from back to front.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Push the needle through and guide it around the edge of the fabric from the back, bringing it back to the front to maintain the wrapping motion.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Pull the needle through to the front, emerging at point 2. The thread wraps around the folded edge, creating the characteristic diagonal whip stitch from point 1 to point 2.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Continue this pattern along the entire torn edge. The front shows a series of evenly spaced, diagonal stitches wrapping over the edge to secure the fold.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: On the back, the thread forms a continuous line along the edge. Tie a secure knot to finish and trim any excess thread. The torn edge is now neatly repaired.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length, depending on the size of the hole you need to repair.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your fabric. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch near the hole.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric from the back side. The needle should emerge on the opposite side, pulling the thread through.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile. The needle emerges at the edge of the hole, completing your first stitch entry.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch at point '1', where the thread has emerged at the edge of the hole.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle downwards at point '2', directly across from where the thread emerged at point '1'.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Push the needle through from point '2' and bring it up at point '3'. You are creating a horizontal stitch across the gap.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Continue the pattern. You can now see two parallel horizontal stitches across the gap, forming the beginning of the ladder.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Repeat the process: the needle goes down at point '2', with the previous stitch at '1' and the next emergence point at '3'.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Continue alternating stitches. Insert the needle at point '4' and push it down to add another stitch across the hole.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: You can now see the parallel stitches spanning across the gap, forming a ladder-like pattern.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.text: Continue building the stitch. The needle emerges at point '5', with previous stitches marked at '3' and '4'.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.text: A series of evenly spaced, parallel stitches are now visible across the entire length of the hole.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.text: Gently pull the working thread as shown. The parallel stitches will draw the edges of the hole together, closing the gap invisibly.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.text: On the front, the hole is now completely closed. The repair appears as a single, neat line, making it virtually invisible.

steps.title: Step 17
steps.text: On the back, the thread forms a continuous line connecting the stitches. Tie a secure knot to finish the repair and trim any excess thread.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: The needle emerges at point 3 on the front. The thread now crosses diagonally from point 1 to point 3, forming the characteristic catch stitch pattern.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Bring the needle back to the original side, positioning it at point 4. Insert the needle, continuing the alternating pattern across the split.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Insert the needle at point 5, pushing it through the fabric from front to back. The needle passes through point 4 on the opposite side, continuing the alternating pattern.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread completely through to the back of the textile, creating another small horizontal stitch on the fabric edge.

steps.text: The needle emerges at point 5 on the front. The thread crosses diagonally from point 4 to point 5, forming another X-shaped stitch that holds the split together.

steps.text: Continue this pattern along the entire split. The front shows a series of evenly spaced, crossing stitches that hold the fabric edges flat without puckering.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.text: Hold the needle in one hand and the thread in the other. Carefully insert the end of the thread through the eye of the needle.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.text: Pull the thread through the needle's eye. Cut the thread to your desired length, depending on the size of the patch.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.text: Position your patch over the damaged area. From the back of the textile, hold the needle ready to begin your first stitch along the edge of the patch.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.text: Push the needle through the fabric and the patch from the back side. The needle should emerge on the front side, pulling the thread through.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.text: Pull the needle and thread through to the front of the textile. The needle emerges, completing your first stitch entry along the patch edge.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.text: On the front, you'll see the first stitch at point 1. Position the needle at point 2, a short distance from point 1, ready to insert it through both the patch and fabric layers.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.text: Insert the needle at point 2, pushing it down through both the patch and fabric layers from front to back.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.text: Push the needle through from point 2 and bring it up at point 3, a short distance ahead. You now have two complete stitches visible on the front.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.text: Pull the thread through completely. The front shows two complete running stitches forming a dashed line along the patch edge.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.text: Continue the pattern: the needle goes down at point 2, with the previous stitch at point 1 and the next emergence point at point 3, creating evenly spaced stitches.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.text: Continue stitching along the entire perimeter of the patch. The front shows the characteristic dashed pattern of evenly spaced stitches holding the patch securely in place.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.text: On the back, the thread forms longer paths connecting the stitches. Tie a secure knot to finish the repair and trim any excess thread.
